sn35.75:6.1: “If, bhikkhu you understand that the Dhamma has not been taught by me for the sake of purification of virtue, then for what purpose do you understand the Dhamma to have been taught by me?”
sn35.75:7.1: “Venerable sir, I understand the Dhamma to have been taught by the Blessed One for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.”
sn35.75:8.2: It is good that you understand the Dhamma to have been taught by me for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.
sn35.75:8.3: For the Dhamma is taught by me for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.
sn35.75:9.2: is the eye permanent or impermanent?”—
sn35.75:11.9: whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—permanent or impermanent?”—
sn35.75:13.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”—
sn35.75:15.1: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.75:15.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”—
sn35.75:17.7: He understands: ‘… there is no more for this state of being.’”
sn35.75:18.1: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn35.75:18.2: Elated, that bhikkhu delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
sn35.75:18.3: And while this discourse was being spoken, that bhikkhu’s mind was liberated from the taints by nonclinging.
